t.en: In the quantifier rules a metavariable is followed by variables: <part-ref to="part:allI"></part-ref> is ⟦⋀x. ?P(x)⟧ ⟹ ∀x. ?P(x). ?P is not a sentence but “a sentence about x”. Solving ∀x. ?P(x) ≐ ∀x. x is human → x is mortal must give ?P ≐ fun x => x is human → x is mortal: ?P is a function with x as its parameter.

When two “for all” are split, both bodies get the same variable, and the equation is marked ⋀x: x is bound by a quantifier. ?A may not take x out with it, so ∀x. ?A ≐ ∀x. x is human has no solution (the occurs check checks this too); ?P(x) may, being about x in the first place. A new part, “Pattern unification”: when ?P is followed by distinct ⋀ variables, it solves ?P.

after.en: When a metavariable is followed only by distinct bound variables, the solution is unique: a <wiki-ref to="pattern"></wiki-ref> (Miller’s patterns).

brief.en: Design a proof assistant that solves each set of equations to the end, or says “failed” when they do not fit or have no solution.

hint.en: Let the unifier do what it can, and pass an equation like ?P(x) that is left to the new part.
Once ?P is solved, there may be more unifying to do.
